chapter_theme: Seeing the Siva-guru (சிவகுரு தரிசனம்): the true guru is Siva himself come into the world, who tests, removes the bonds and shows the soul, the bonds and the Lord; siddhi, release and the knowledge of Vedanta cannot be known except by his grace, and fools who take him for an ordinary man miss it.
structure_note: 1573 to 1578 define the Siva-guru by what he does; 1579 to 1587 insist that every attainment comes through his grace, with 1581 as the summary 'the guru is Siva'; 1588 and 1589 close in the first person, with the speaker's own release.

1573.reading: Making one bow in devotion, giving the feet to praise, testing with pure teaching so that fault is removed, and showing the real, the unreal and the real-unreal: because he does this, the guru who is mind and Lord is the Siva-guru.
1573.nuance: சத்து, அசத்து, சதசத்து (sat, asat, sadasat) are traditionally the Lord, the bonds and the soul, which is neither wholly real nor unreal but takes the nature of what it joins. சித்தம் இறையே is unclear: 'the mind is the Lord' or 'the guru whose mind is the Lord'.

1574.reading: Gathering the bonds, binding them and plucking them out, freeing one from the cherished body, and directly joining one to release without shame: the faultless true guru with this aim is the hall itself.
1574.nuance: அம்பலம், the hall, is the dance hall of Chidambaram, so the guru is equated with the place of the Lord's dance; it may also be read as the open space of consciousness. கூசற்ற முத்தி is release without shrinking or shame.

1575.reading: The eight siddhis, the purification that makes one firmly Siva, the purity of the eight powers, the power in yoga, the knowledge of mantra practice and devotion: all are learned by the Lord's grace.
1575.nuance: எண்சத்தி, the eight powers, may be the Lord's eight shaktis or the eight siddhis again. நாதன் here is the Lord, who in this chapter is the guru.

1576.reading: Because he who is beyond all the worlds comes here, gives abundant grace in the hearts of the good, and takes everyone to save them and protects them, the good guru praised in words is pure Siva.
1576.nuance: அப்பாலோன் இப்பாலாய், the one beyond becoming the one here, is the chapter's whole doctrine of the guru in four words.

1577.reading: God, the pure guru and the means: by teaching you to see everything as these three, and removing the unaging bond of soul and fetter, the supreme guru in love gives everything that belongs to release.
1577.nuance: தேவன், சுத்த குரு, உபாயம் (God, guru, means) is one triad; the verse may also mean seeing everything as the three categories of Pati, pasu and pasam. மூவாப் பசுபாசம் is the soul's beginningless bondage.

1578.reading: The utter fools who do not see the grace pure Siva gives by coming as guru and purifying say 'he is one of us, with eyes that deceive'; the meritorious bow at his feet, saying 'this is the Father'.
1578.nuance: பொய்த்தகு கண்ணான் நமர் is obscure: perhaps 'a man of ours, seen by deceived eyes', the fools mistaking the guru for an ordinary man. The verse sets two ways of seeing the same person.

1579.reading: Removing falsehood by truth, the firmness of the world of truth, the bounty of Hara who is bright Siva, and the bewilderment of the sixty-four siddhis: who knows these except by the Lord's grace?
1579.nuance: எட்டெட்டுச் சித்தி may be sixty-four or eight and eight. மயக்கம் may mean the siddhis' power to bewilder, a warning against them, or the bewildering wonder of them.

1580.reading: Because Siva himself is the Siva-jnani, those who can reach his feet saying 'pure Siva' gain the good release of the new tattva; there is no more becoming, and there is the supreme world.
1580.nuance: சிவஞானி is the guru as knower of Siva, here said to be Siva himself. நவமான தத்துவம் may be 'the new tattva' or 'the ninefold tattva'.

1581.reading: Nandi said the guru is Siva; people do not grasp that the guru is Siva; the guru stands as Siva and as king; the guru is a king beyond word and thought.
1581.nuance: குருவே opens every line. The teaching is given on Nandi's authority, the guru of Tirumular's own line.

1582.reading: All that is thought abides in thinking; by grace one is made to know the meaning; when the whole mind becomes firmly Siva, the Father settles right there.
1582.nuance: சித்த யாவையும் is unclear and may be a slip for சித்தம் யாவையும், which opens line 3. அத்தம் is 'meaning' and அத்தன் 'the Father': the verse plays on the two.

1583.reading: No one knows the intent of Nandi, the king and our father, who set the glory met within his own glory; to one who rejoices calling him the Nandi of the sky, he becomes the solitary flame of fire at dusk.
1583.nuance: The verse plays on நந்தி and அந்தி (dusk) and is largely opaque. அங்கித் தனிச்சுடர் (the lone flame of fire) recalls the inner light of yoga; the sense I give is a guess.

1584.reading: The holy siddhi and release, the grace that grants glory without bewilderment, and the knowledge of Vedanta that is the truthful meaning ending delusion cannot be known unless the Lord takes form and gives grace.
1584.nuance: நாதன் உருவாய், the Lord taking form, is the guru: knowledge of Vedanta is not reached by study alone.

1585.reading: Devotion and the knowledge that is dispassion are the seed of the supreme siddhi; because one joins 'I am Siva', the knowledge of release sprouts; and if Shakti gives grace, that sprout grows easily.
1585.nuance: சிவோகம், 'I am Siva', is a meditation in which the self is identified with Siva; whether this is a practice or the state reached is unclear. The seed and sprout image echoes 1932.

1586.reading: Our Lord, the First One, who set before me the blissful birth to be attained later, reveals himself when his time comes; it is the mind he set to be held steady.
1586.nuance: இன்பப் பிறப்பு, a blissful birth, may be the new birth given by the guru's initiation. The last line is unclear: perhaps the Lord appears as, or in, the mind made steady.

1587.reading: Clear Siva-knowledge is bright siddhi; clear Siva-knowledge is bright release; Siva-knowledge goes as one into the supreme Siva; Siva-knowledge gives Siva's bliss.
1587.nuance: சிவமான ஞானம் opens every line. The verse makes Siva-knowledge itself the attainments that 1575 and 1584 list separately.

1588.reading: I have known and understood this whole wide world; understanding closely and reciting, I gained holy grace; I have forgotten and left the life of those whose wits are dead; I was born and have ended this birth.
1588.nuance: பிறந்தொழிந்தேன் means 'I was born and am done', so this birth is the last. மதி மாண்டவர் (those whose understanding has died) are the worldly the speaker has left behind.

1589.reading: People do not understand at all how the Lord of all the many lives he sustains is present; cutting away this dividing quarrel, I saw the Lord who holds everything as in a womb.
1589.nuance: பிரிக்கின்ற பிணக்கு, the quarrel that divides, may be the sense of separation between soul and Lord or the sects' disputes of chapter 106. கருக்கொண்ட, having conceived, makes the Lord the womb of all.

links.note: Both use seed and sprout. 1932 makes them the inseparable cause and effect that reveal Hara's way; 1585 makes devotion and dispassion the seed and release-knowledge the sprout, which Shakti's grace makes grow.
1576 argues that the guru is pure Siva because the one beyond the worlds comes here and saves; 1581 states it flatly on Nandi's word and adds that people fail to grasp it.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if it doesn't lead to the Lord's feet; Tirumular says even the knowledge of Vedanta cannot be known unless the Lord comes as guru. Learning is not enough in either, but for Tirumular the grace must come first.

1574 calls the guru who gathers and plucks out the bonds (பாசத்தைக் கூட்டியே கட்டிப் பறித்திட்டு) and joins one to release ஆசற்ற சற்குரு; 2052 gives the same title, ஆசற்ற சற்குரு, to those who remove the bond (பாசத்தை நீக்கி) and drive out impurity. Read together, the faultless true guru is defined in both places by one act, ending the bond, and 2052 adds the contrast with the guru moved by clamour.

1575 says the eight siddhis, yogic power and mantra knowledge are all learned by the Lord's grace (நாதன் அருளிற் பயிலுமே); Thiruppugazh 194 says what comes from knowing Murugan as the gem does not come by mercury and the like (இரதாதிகளால்), the alchemist's nine metals. Both deny that powers are won by technique and place them in grace, one against yoga and mantra, the other against alchemy.

115 lays down that pasu and pasam are beginningless like Pati and cannot reach Pati, but do not remain when Pati draws near (பதியணுகிற் பசு பாசம் நில்லாவே); 1577 names the guru as the one who removes the unaging bond of soul and fetter (மூவாப் பசுபாசம் மாற்றியே). The pairing shows the guru as the form in which Pati's drawing near happens.

1578 says fools look at Siva come as guru and see only one of themselves (நமர்), while the meritorious say 'this is the Father'; Kural 1071 says the base look exactly like human beings (மக்களே போல்வர் கயவர்). Both turn on human likeness misleading the eye, in opposite directions: in the Kural the man-shape hides less than a man, in Tirumular it hides Siva. The pairing depends on reading பொய்த்தகு கண்ணான் நமர் as mistaking the guru for an ordinary man.

1580 says Siva himself is the Siva-jnani (சிவனே சிவஞானி), so those who reach his feet gain release and the supreme world; 1909 describes the Siva-jnani in whose heart grace dwells, for whom Siva is everywhere and who, dying here, stands everywhere as the Lord. 1580 makes the knower Siva from Siva's side; 1909 shows the same identity from the knower's side.

A near-repeat: 1586 and 1629 have the same four lines (பின்னெய்த வைத்ததோர் இன்பப் பிறப்பினை ... மன்னெய்த வைத்த மனமது தானே), with only spelling differences. Placed in the chapter on the Siva-guru and again in the chapter on tapas, the verse about the Lord revealing himself in his time to the steadied mind is read once as the guru's work and once as the fruit of tapas.

1587 opens every line with சிவமான ஞானம் and makes Siva-knowledge itself siddhi, release and Siva's bliss; 1598 opens every line with திருவடி ஞானம் and makes knowledge of the feet itself Siva-hood, Sivaloka, freedom from mala and 'firm siddhi and release'. The two verses have the same form and the same claim, and set side by side they show that 'knowledge of Siva' and 'knowledge of the feet' are used as one thing.

1588: 'I have known and understood (அறிந்துணர்ந்தேன்) ... I was born and have ended this birth (பிறந்தொழிந்தேன்)'; Kural 356: those who have learned here and seen the true thing (கற்றீண்டு மெய்ப்பொருள் கண்டார்) reach the path of not coming back (மற்றீண்டு வாரா நெறி). The Kural states as a rule what Tirumular claims in the first person: knowing here ends the return to birth.

A near-repeat: 1589 and 1782 share all four lines (தரிக்கின்ற பல்லுயிர்க்கு எல்லாந் தலைவன் ... கருக்கொண்ட ஈசனைக் கண்டுகொண்டேனே) except that 1589 reads பிரிக்கின்ற இந்தப் பிணக்கு, 'this dividing quarrel', where 1782 reads பிரிக்கின்ற விந்து பிணக்கு, 'the strife of the dividing bindu'. The variant decides whether the obstacle to seeing the Lord who holds all as in a womb is a quarrel of views or the yogic bindu.

source_issues: 1582: line 1 reads சித்த யாவையும், probably for சித்தம் யாவையும் as in line 3.
1583: largely obscure; the play on நந்தி and அந்தி may hide a corruption.
